summary: Project Git's Children presents Nalix: Earth System Trend Detective, an interactive scientific web platform that detects, quantifies, and validates multi-decadal climate regime shifts and wildfire dynamics across Bolivia using over 40 years of NASA satellite and reanalysis observations. Addressing the challenge of separating true environmental signals from natural climate noise, our platform fuses NASA POWER (MERRA-2, 1981–2025) hydro-climatic series with NASA FIRMS (MODIS, 2003–2025) active fire hotspots. Through an intuitive three-tier workspace—a regional Drought & Wildfire Workstation (/analisis and /regiones) and an arbitrary-coordinate Statistical Investigation Lab (/investigation)—the system executes autocorrelation-corrected Hamed-Rao Mann-Kendall tests, Theil-Sen robust slopes, Benjamini-Hochberg False Discovery Rate (FDR) control, Pettitt and CUSUM change-point detection, Z-score anomaly ranking, and lagged Spearman correlations. Nalix empowers scientists, policymakers, and communities in vulnerable ecosystems like Santa Cruz and the Chiquitanía to answer what is changing, where, how fast, and whether it is statistically significant.
details:
1. WHAT IT DOES & HOW IT WORKS

Project Git's Children (Nalix: Earth System Trend Detective) transforms complex multi-decadal satellite records into rigorous, accessible scientific answers for four core Earth system detective questions:

- What is changing? Multi-variable tracking across temperature, precipitation, humidity, evapotranspiration, soil moisture, and active fire anomalies.

- Where is it changing? Multi-scale spatial coverage across Bolivia's 9 departments, ecological macro-regions, 0.5° x 0.5° satellite grid cells, and any user-selected coordinate or municipality.

- How much / how fast is it changing? Robust parametric (OLS slope with 95% confidence intervals) and non-parametric (Theil-Sen median slope in units/decade) quantification.

- Is the change statistically significant? Autocorrelation-adjusted p-values (Hamed-Rao modified Mann-Kendall) combined with Benjamini-Hochberg False Discovery Rate (FDR q-values) to eliminate false positives across multi-indicator comparisons.

The live application (https://earth-system-trend-web.vercel.app) is organized into three cohesive modules:

A) Nalix Visual Portal (/): Interactive entry point introducing Bolivia's thermal and hydro-climatic stress context.

B) Regional Drought & Wildfire Workstation (/analisis & /regiones): Connects 44+ years of NASA POWER (MERRA-2, 1981–2025) across 6 core hydro-climatic indicators (Max Temperature T2M_MAX, Corrected Precipitation PRECTOTCORR, 2m Relative Humidity RH2M, Evapotranspiration Flux EVPTRNS, Surface Soil Wetness GWETTOP, and Root-Zone Soil Wetness GWETROOT) with 22+ years of NASA FIRMS (MODIS Collection 6.1, 2003–2025) fire hotspots (88,600+ aggregated spatial-temporal cell records). Users can filter by season (Annual, Dry Season May–Oct, and Fire Peak Jul–Nov) to inspect:

- Concurrent Drought-Fire Coupling (/api/link): Spearman rank correlation (rho) and p-values testing how atmospheric desiccation and heat anomalies drive active fire counts and radiative power (FRP).

- Seasonal Early-Warning Lead Analysis (/api/lead): Tests whether antecedent wet-season (Nov–Apr) precipitation and soil moisture deficits anticipate the severity of the subsequent wildfire season.

C) Deep Statistical Investigation Lab (/investigation): Powered by our custom scientific math engine (sci_lab_math), allowing users to click any point on the interactive Leaflet map or search any Bolivian locality via OpenStreetMap Nominatim. It runs an automated statistical pipeline including:

- Trend Detection: Ordinary Least Squares (OLS), Classic Mann-Kendall, Hamed-Rao Autocorrelation-Corrected Mann-Kendall, and Theil-Sen Robust Estimator.

- Structural Regime Shifts: Non-parametric Pettitt test, Cumulative Sum (CUSUM), and PELT structural break detection to pinpoint the exact year a climate regime shifted.

- Extreme Events & Dynamics: Z-Score and IQR anomaly ranking, Lagged Cross-Correlation (CCF), Fast Fourier Transform (FFT) seasonality decomposition, and spatial PCA + K-Means regional clustering, synthesized into an automated human-readable scientific verdict.

2. BENEFITS & INTENDED IMPACT

National climate averages often hide localized regime shifts in critical South American biomes such as Santa Cruz de la Sierra, the Chiquitanía dry forest, the Bolivian Amazon, the Chaco, and the Andean Altiplano. By uniting rigorous statistical validation (Hamed-Rao + FDR control) with actionable fire-drought coupling, Nalix helps environmental agencies, agricultural planners, civil defense teams, and citizens distinguish temporary weather fluctuations from structural climate degradation—supporting early wildfire prevention and water resource adaptation.

3. TOOLS, CODING LANGUAGES, HARDWARE & SOFTWARE ARCHITECTURE

- Backend & Scientific Engine: Python 3.10+, FastAPI, Uvicorn, NumPy, SciPy, Pandas, Statsmodels, Scikit-Learn, Ruptures, PyKrige, and HTTPX. Engineered with a dual-engine architecture (full scientific stack + pure-Python serverless statistical engine) and a two-tier caching system (pre-warmed NASA POWER JSON cache in backend/.cache/ with automatic /tmp/.cache/ serverless fallback).

- Frontend & Geospatial UI: Next.js 15 (App Router), React 19, TypeScript, Mantine UI v7, Recharts, and Leaflet / React-Leaflet with GeoBolivia administrative boundaries and custom spatial heat/grid overlays.

- Cloud Deployment & QA Pipeline: Deployed on Vercel (Serverless Python API + Edge/SSR Next.js Frontend), validated with Pytest unit suites, automated Playwright 1080p browser capture, Microsoft Edge-TTS neural narration, and FFmpeg audio-visual mastering.

4. CREATIVITY & SCIENTIFIC FACTORS CONSIDERED

- Solving the Autocorrelation Trap: Environmental time series exhibit strong lag-1 serial correlation, causing standard Mann-Kendall tests to inflate false positives. Our team implemented the Hamed & Rao (1998) variance correction using effective sample size (n*) and paired it with Benjamini-Hochberg FDR across all 6 indicators simultaneously.

- Bridging Climate Reanalysis and Active Wildfires: Instead of viewing temperature trends in isolation, we built a statistical bridge linking MERRA-2 soil/atmospheric moisture deficits directly to MODIS 0.5° gridded fire radiative power and hotspot counts.

- Zero-Failure Serverless Resilience: To guarantee instant response times for judges without hitting external NASA API rate limits, we pre-warmed 54 regional indicator matrices across all 9 Bolivian departments and embedded 88,663 monthly MODIS fire grid records directly into the repository.

5. SUPER INTELLIGENCE (SI) TRANSPARENCY & METADATA DISCLOSURE

In full compliance with NASA Space Apps Challenge 2026 Super Intelligence (SI) guidelines:

- Code & Documentation: AI coding assistants (Devin, OpenCode, and Google Gemini) were utilized to accelerate full-stack scaffolding, TypeScript/FastAPI route wiring, serverless optimization, and technical documentation. All statistical algorithms execute deterministically via verified mathematical equations over real NASA datasets.

- Video & Visual Watermarks: Our 28-second project demonstration video (https://youtu.be/avhOwPCravI) displays a permanent, visible watermark overlay ("SI-Assisted Demo | AI Voiceover | Git's Children") throughout the entire video, and the landing page background visual (front/public/nalix-calor.mp4) retains its visible generator watermark ("Dreamina AI"). Zero NASA logos, insignias, or branding elements were generated or modified.

- Audio & Voiceover Metadata: The 28-second demonstration narration was generated using neural Text-to-Speech (Microsoft Edge-TTS voice en-US-AndrewNeural / es-BO-MarceloNeural) mixed with a 100% copyright-free ambient harmonic pad mathematically synthesized via FFmpeg (aevalsrc sine-wave generator).
